The Regional Thematic Specialist will also lead the CAD RTU, which will provide thematic oversight and support on regional efforts to address the immediate and long-term impacts of climate change on human mobility while advocating sustainable and inclusive solutions on a regional scale in collaboration with CAD HQ. Special focus will be placed on leveraging IOM’s expertise and role in the new Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage and access to climate financing and technical support to Member States on National Adaptation Plans (NAP) and National Determination Commitments (NDC), especially for Small Islands Developing States and Least Developed Countries that experience interconnected social, environmental and economic challenges. The CAD RTU will also identify regional opportunities and risks, foster knowledge sharing, encourage policy and research development, and support cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the CAD RTU offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners in the Region, the CAD RTU is the go-to source for climate action and mobility expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. **Strategic Direction:** Lead and manage the CAD RTU in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the strategic plan.

2\. **Advocacy and Representation:** Assist and provide substantive inputs to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's strategic plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on CAD HQ and Global Offices' (GO) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. **Technical Assistance:** Lead the CAD RTU's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with CAD HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on Climate change and human mobility, protection, life-saving actions, and recovery.

4\. **Training and Capacity Development:**  
a. In coordination with CAD HQ and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.  
b. Spearhead the consultation, development, consensus-building, implementation, and oversight of global Climate migration and displacement governance frameworks across member states, international organizations, and civil society on the global stage.  
c. In coordination with and in support of COs, strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of national governments and local actors to absorb, account for, report on, allocate, and leverage climate finance effectively.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. **Strategic Partnerships:** Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. **Resource Mobilization:** In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnerships and Advocacy (COPAs), COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. **Project Development and Reporting:** In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook.

8\. **Monitoring and Evaluation:** In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring, and Evaluation Officer (RPMEO), hold regular bilateral discussions with COs thematic focal points to assess challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff, and guide CO adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback.

9\. **Risk Management:** In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

**Climate Action Policy and Research:**

10\. **Knowledge Management and Innovation:** In coordination with the RPDO and Climate Mobility Innovation Labs Unit, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate Climate Action innovative and best practices related to CAD.

11\. **Policy:**  
a. Promote policy coherence and inclusive partnerships to mainstream climate mobility in relevant agendas, including biodiversity, water management, mountains, oceans/seas, human rights, protection, security, gender, health, urbanization, SDGs, youth engagement, diaspora empowerment, local actors’ mobilization.  
b. Scale up advocacy, policy, and partnership in early warning (EW4AI), and climate and environmental action at policy and advocacy levels, in support of priorities identified by affected countries in national or regional and global climate strategies.  
c. Support CAD HQ in the mainstreaming of human mobility considerations in climate change, environmental and disaster policy agendas, including via its work on UNFCCC Constituted Bodies, Workstreams, Initiatives and Fora (WIM Excom, AC, SNLD, COP, NAPs, NDCs, climate funds, etc.), as well as the UNCCD, UNEA and Sendai Framework policy processes, and the engagement with the Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF).

12\. **Data, Research, and Foresight:** In coordination with different climate change fora including UNFCCC, IPCC, IDMC and others in collaboration with CAD HQ, as well as the Global Data Institute (GDI), and the Regional Data Hub (RDH), analyse and disseminate Climate Action thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

13\. **Thematic Community of Practice:** Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of CAD HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

14\. **Coordination:** Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTS, Global Thematic Specialists (GTS), and COs focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

15\. **Mainstream:** In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities in all areas of CAD’s work in the Region. Furthermore, promote the integration of Climate Action at RO and CO levels to enhance programme leadership, strategy, design and implementation across all thematic areas.

**CAD Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

16\. Manage the CAD Regional Thematic Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the CAD RTU Terms of Reference.

17\. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the [UNESCO World Higher Education Database](https://whed.net/home.php).

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in climate action and mobility, and related areas relevant to project development and management, thematic capacity building, and liaison;
- Minimum 5 years' experience working in non-OECD countries managing climate action and mobility projects;
- Experience in liaison, resource mobilization, and advocacy with governmental and diplomatic officials, national and international institutions and organizations, civil society, and private sector actors;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organization, the United Nations, or government; and,
- Experience in the design and implementation of capacity building on climate action and mobility.

**Skills**

- Ability to understand complex contexts and fast-changing migration and displacement dynamics and ability to frame them in their regional, global, and political contexts;
- Proven track record of successful engagement with donors, developing projects, and mobilizing resources for IOM priority areas;
- Demonstrated ability to effectively lead and manage a diverse teams of specialists;
- Strong analytical skills combined with the ability to effectively summarize, present, and communicate findings;
- Demonstrated knowledge and expertise of relevant international standards and classifications relevant to climate action and mobility; and,
- Proven agent of change or willingness to foster a culture of learning and knowledge management.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 22519 Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) (P)
body:
The Transition and Recovery (TR) Pillar of the Somalia Country Office plays a leading role in stabilisation strategy and delivery throughout Somalia. The Community Stabilisation programme is central to the United Nations (UN) Country Team’s plans for transition and closure of the UN’s political mission in Somalia. The main objective of the unit is to lead coordinated stabilisation efforts across the international community, aligned with the core objectives of the Government of Somalia.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office in Nairobi/Senior Programme Coordinator (Transition & Recovery Pillar) and the direct supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator (Community Stabilisation), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) at the Regional Office (RO) for Eastern and Southern Africa in Nairobi and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters (HQ), the Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will be responsible and accountable for managing, coordinating and overseeing the activities of the European Union flagship stabilisation project: Strengthening the Social Contract through Socio-Economic Infrastructure (2026-2029), and its integration with the FCDO flagship project: Strengthening Community Security and Stabilisation (SCSS). The Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will support the coordination and collaboration across relevant Transition and Recovery initiatives while maintaining responsibility and accountability for the management and implementation of the Community Stabilisation portfolio.

The Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will coordinate and maintain effective working relationships with relevant government counterparts, donors, United Nations agencies, implementing partners and other stakeholders to support programme implementation and achieve programme objectives. The Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will coordinate technical-level engagement and collaboration with the Government of Somalia at Federal (FGS) and Member State (FMS) levels, with a primary focus on the Ministry of Interior. The Programme Manager (Coomunity Stabilisation) will support coordination and information sharing among relevant stabilisation stakeholders to promote effective programme implementation and collaboration.

The Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will be responsible and accountable for programme development and implementation, including but not limited to monitoring, reporting, projectization, staff supervision, and advancement of new initiatives within the Programme and in the global context. In addition, the Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will actively contribute to IOM’s country-level programming, including the design, implementation, oversight of projects, and coordination within and across the IOM Somalia Mission. The Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will provide technical stabilisation support and advice for the development of strategic plans for the Country Office (CO) and Regional Office (RO).

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee the effective development and implementation of the Community Stabilisation programme by exercising administrative, operational and financial management responsibility for relevant projects, in particular the integration between two key flagship projects (funded by EU-INTPA and FCDO respectively), ensuring effective coordination and complementarity among relevant programme activities and projects.
2. Provide operational management, technical supervision, mentorship, and capacity-building support to Community Stabilisation staff, assisting on programmatic strategy, resource allocation, and staff contributions to the CO's strategic priorities.
3. Establish, maintain, and further expand strong relationships across UN Agencies, humanitarian organizations, government and community interlocutors, and with a broad range of other local interests toward the successful implementation of the Community Stabilisation programme.
4. Identify the priorities arising during the implementation of the Programme and coordinate the design and contribute to the development of the new projects under the Programme and activities based on a solid results framework and in response to emerging trends and priorities, as well as donor interests and requirements, in close coordination with the COM, Regional Office, relevant Units at HQ, as well as with Government counterparts and other relevant public/private sector’s partner organizations.
5. Ensure that the key programmatic directions are shared with international stakeholders, including donors, to maximize impact, minimize overlapping, and stimulate funds mobilization for the new programmes.
6. Ensure timely, quality preparation, compilation, and submission of programme reports, updates, and briefs for donors, government, and other stakeholders, in close coordination with relevant units and programme staff, and in compliance with IOM and donor requirements and procedures.
7. Oversee the M&E framework including the development, dissemination, and regular update of assessment and monitoring tools, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and data collection and analysis mechanisms in coordination with the CO's M&E Officer, monitoring progress against strategic objectives and benchmarks and sharing relevant information with humanitarian community partners.
8. Ensure that the objectives set in programme documents and budgets, M&E frameworks and work plans are compliant with IOM’s organizational policies and donors’ contractual requirements, interests and expectations.
9. Oversee the production of visibility/communications materials in close coordination with the Public Information Officer/Focal Point of the CO.
10. Participate and engage actively at relevant donor or partner meetings, briefings and conferences at the international and national level.
11. Undertake travel duties nationally or internationally, as required, including regular visits to Sub-Offices, to coordinate, develop and/or support programme implementation.
12. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Humanitarian Affairs, Economic Development, Social Sciences, Humanities, Business Administration, Public Administration, International Studies, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in stabilisation, transition and recovery, peacebuilding, or related programming;
- Experience in project development, implementation, monitoring, reporting and evaluation;
- Experience liaising with governmental authorities, development partners, donors and international organizations;
- Familiarity with financial and administrative management;
- Experience working in fragile or complex operational environments is an advantage; and,
- Experience managing stabilisation and peace projects under the Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) and Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF).

**Skills**

- Proven ability to establish and maintain strong working relations with relevant Government counterparts, international organizations and private sector entities;
- Excellent leadership, coordination, and information management skills;
- Detailed knowledge of the UN System, NGOs and other international organizations/institutions;
- Knowledge of migration data, labour migration patterns in the Horn of Africa and ability to negotiate with government authorities;
- Good knowledge of human and financial resources management;
- Strong conceptualization, analytical and writing skills;
- Strong communication, organizational and interpersonal relationship skills;
- Ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure with minimum supervision; and,
- Ability to establish and maintain partnerships with development partners, government counterparts, UN agencies, local authorities and other relevant stakeholders.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Expression of Interest: Procurement of a Loans Management System for a Rural Based Informal MFI
body:
**Organization:** World Vision Somalia (SomReP)

**Project:** SERECA

**Donor Funded:** ANCP

**Position Type:** Contract

**Location:** Remote & in Somalia/Land (Dollow and Elefyne)

**Estimated working days:** 60 days

**Estimated number of staff required to work on the project:** 1-5

**Reporting to:** Economic Development and Market System Development Advisor - SomReP

**Starting Date:** Oct 2026

**Background**

The Somalia Resilience Programme (SomReP) is a consortium of seven international non-governmental organizations (INGO) and one Local NGO. SomReP works to enhance the resilience of chronically vulnerable households, communities and systems across Somalia.

The Somalia Resilience Program (SomReP) is an ambitious approach to tackle the challenge of recurrent droughts and the chronic vulnerability among pastoralists, agro-pastoralists, and peri-urban households in one of the poorest countries in the world. SomReP is being implemented through a consortium of 7 INGOs (ACF, ADRA, CARE, COOPI, DRC, Oxfam and WVI) and 1 Local NGO (Shaqodoon)

Through Somalia Enhanced Resilience through Inclusive Economic/Market Systems development and Climate Smart Approaches (SERECA), SomReP would like to engage a qualified and dynamic consultant to support development Loans Management System for a rural based informal MFI

District bank committee (DBC) is a rural-based informal microfinance model committed to providing affordable financial services to underserved communities in Dollow and Elefyne. To improve efficiency, transparency, and client service, SOMREP seeks to acquire a robust Loans Management System (LMS) for the DBC that support its operations.

**Objective**

To procure and implement a secure, scalable, and user-friendly LMS that automates the loan lifecycle from application to repayment while integrating with mobile money platforms and supporting offline field operations.

**Scope of Work**

The selected vendor will be required to:

- Develop, supply, install, and configure the LMS.
- Migrate existing loan and client data.
- Integrate with **Mobile money platforms** and other relevant payment channels.
- Enable offline data capture for field officers with automatic sync.
- Provide role-based access control and audit trails.
- Generate customizable reports (portfolio, arrears, compliance, etc.).
- Train staff and provide user manuals.
- Offer ongoing technical support and system updates.
- Complete systems handover, but maintain technical support

**Key Features Required**

- Loan Origination & Approval Workflow in line with credit policies
- Client Management & KYC Compliance in line with the regulation
- Automated Repayment Scheduling & Alerts
- Portfolio at Risk (PAR) Tracking 0-30 days/normal, 30-90 days/watch, 91-180days/Substandard, 181-360days doubtful, above 36 days/loss
- Portfolio automated reporting
- Multi-branch & Multi-currency Support
- Data Security & Backup Mechanisms

**Deliverables**

- Fully functional LMS meeting agreed specifications.
- Data migration report.
- Training completion report.
- System documentation and user manuals.
- Post-implementation support plan.
- Train credit officers and DBC credit committee on the use of the LMS.
- Validation of the installed system by stakeholders

**Timeline**

The project is expected to be completed within **60 days** from contract signing.

**Reporting and Communication**

The consultant will report to the Economic development and Market systems advisor and other SOMREP implementing partners. The consultant is expected to update advisor on a regular basis and submit progress reports according to an agreed schedule. Any issues, delays, or obstacles should be communicated promptly to ensure timely resolution.

**Vendor Qualifications**

- 10 years proven experience in implementing LMS for microfinance/Sacco’s in rural contexts.
- Masters degree in related Management information systems development like Computer science, Software engineering, IT and related area
- Demonstrated capacity for mobile money integration.
- Strong after-sales support.

**Proposal Submission & Evaluation Criteria**

The Selection of the firm will be made based on cumulative analysis (i.e., mandatory requirement and technical qualifications as follows

**Mandatory requirements**

- Copy of business registration (company/organization) s.
- Copy of the tax registration
- Successful bidder will be required to sign World Vision Supplier Code of Conduct form

**Technical Evaluation**

Applicants need to clearly articulate on the following, but not limited to:

**Criteria and Scoring (Total Score = 100%)**

1. **CVs and experience** - 10 years proven experience in implementing LMS for microfinance/Sacco’s in rural contexts. Master’s degree in related Management information systems development like Computer science, Software engineering, IT and related area. Demonstrated capacity for mobile money integration. Strong after-sales support. - (score - 20%).
2. **Systems Technical compliance** - System security, reliability and trustworthiness for the developed systems. This also involves adhering to relevant laws, regulations, standards and guidelines relevant to the industry, including all compliance like certifications etc. - (score - 20%)
3. **Clear work plan including time frames the consulting firm will undertake to finalize the assignment as per the scope of work** - (score - 15%).
4. **Consulting firm profile/cover letter** (Not exceeding two pages) - (score -15%).
5. **Up to two-page statement of capability (referencing the selection criteria) and the approach to be take in undertaking this assignment as per the scope of work, including relevant experience and at least 2 samples of similar work done.** - (score - 20%).
6. **Support and training plan** - (score - 10%).

**More Details to be provided in the full ToR upon Expression of Interest.**

**We hereby invite Expression of Interest from registered, approved and reputable consultants to provide above-named services to World Vision Somalia.**

title: Development of E-Learning Module Content — Tdh Migration and Displacement programme
body:
## **1. Background**

Terre des hommes (Tdh) is Switzerland's largest child rights organisation, active in over 30 countries. Its Migration and Displacement sector has developed two evidence-based Models of Action (MoA) to guide Tdh staff and partners working with migrant, displaced and at-risk children and youth:

**MoA 1 — Employability and access to employment for young migrants and refugees:** Employability and access to employment through (1) Skills and capabilities development, (2) Labour market linkage, and (3) Policy and system strengthening.

**MoA 2 — Education for children and youth on the move:** Structured around the 4As (Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, Adaptability), leading to empowerment and socio-economic (re)integration.

Tdh wishes to make these frameworks accessible to its staff and implementing partners through the **development of related self-paced e-learning modules**. Tdh already runs a Migration and Displacement e-learning course for staff: the two new modules will be produced in the same format and uploaded to the existing platform by Tdh. This assignment covers content development only as platform integration is handled internally.

## **2. Objective and scope of work**

The consultant will develop content for two standalone e-learning modules, one for each MoA. The modules are intended for individual, self-paced learners. For each module, the consultant will submit a complete Word script that Tdh's technical team can upload to the existing CYM e-learning platform. The assignment does not include visual design, coding, platform configuration or upload work

**2.1 Consultant deliverables**

For each of the two modules, the consultant will deliver the following:

- Full content script (Word document): A complete, structured module script covering all learning content, activities and resources. The script must follow the format of the existing Tdh Migration and Development module series and be clear enough for Tdh's technical team to translate it into the online platform. It must include section text, activity instructions, external resource links with precise timecodes where relevant, correct answers for exercises, definitions and call-out boxes. It must be sufficiently clear and structured for the technical team to identify content blocks, activity types, correct answers, feedback text and any resources to be embedded or linked.
- Glossary: A list of 10-15 key terms with concise, learner-friendly definitions tailored to the thematic focus of the module.
- Learner summary sheet: A one-page printable reference sheet summarising the module's key concepts and takeaways, suitable for download alongside the module.
- Review and revision: The consultant will take part in an iterative review process, incorporate consolidated feedback from Tdh and submit revised versions until the module content is validated within the agreed workplan and timeline.

**2.2 Module format, components and minimum requirements**

Existing Migration and Development module scripts will be shared with the selected consultant as a formatting and style reference at the start of the assignment. Each module should follow the expected approach and minimum requirements below.

**Component**

1. Learner experience. **Expected approach:** Individual, self-paced learning. Content should be structured into short thematic sections that combine explanation, examples and activities. **Minimum requirement per module:** 45–60 minutes of learning time.
2. Narrative and voice. **Expected approach:** Write directly to the individual learner in the second person, using a clear and accessible register suitable for practitioners with varied educational backgrounds and operating contexts. **Minimum requirement per module** : Consistent second-person learner voice throughout the script.
3. Script length.**Expected approach :** Provide enough detail for direct platform integration, including all section text, activity instructions, answer keys and feedback text. **Minimum requirement per module** 2,500–4,000 words, including activity instructions and answers.
4. External resources. **Expected approach :** Curate publicly accessible, up-to-date and directly relevant resources, such as short videos, interactive data tools, websites, maps, reports or other practical materials. For any video used, provide precise start and end timecodes.**Minimum requirement per module** : Relevant external resources selected according to the learning objectives and availability of suitable materials. Each resource must include guided comprehension questions and correct answers where appropriate.
5. Interactive activities.**Expected approach :** Embed activities throughout the script and describe them clearly for platform build. Suitable formats include flip cards, matching or association exercises, multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions and open reflection prompts. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 interactive activities, plus at least 1 open reflection prompt. Correct answers and short feedback text must be provided where relevant.
6. Case studies.**Expected approach :** Use real-world or fictionalised case studies grounded in Tdh field contexts, including Asia, Africa and Europe/MENA where relevant. Cases should include named fictional or anonymised characters and guided analysis questions. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.
7. Glossary and key concepts. **Expected approach :** Define core terms in concise, learner-friendly language and use call-out boxes to reinforce critical concepts, legal definitions, common misconceptions and section takeaways.**Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.

## **3. Required profile**

## **Mandatory**

- Demonstrated experience writing e-learning content scripts or instructional materials for NGO or UN audiences
- Strong ability to translate programmatic frameworks into clear, engaging learning content for individual practitioners
- Capacity to identify and integrate high-quality external resources (videos, data tools, reports) into a structured learning narrative
- Substantive knowledge in at least one of the two thematic areas: youth employability, education in emergencies / migration
- Excellent written English; ability to write in a direct, accessible register suitable for diverse field staff

### **Advantageous**

- Familiarity with child rights frameworks and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
- Knowledge of all two thematic areas covered by the MoAs

title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
body:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Uganda dataset.

3\. Transition & Data Collection – Kenya – Weeks 5–7

Key activities

· Close out any outstanding Uganda data collection activities.

· Uganda findings first draft submission

· Transition/travel from Uganda to Kenya.

· Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in Kenya.

· Maintain ongoing data quality assurance and stakeholder debriefs.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

· Complete Kenya fieldwork and initial data checks.

Deliverables

· Uganda fieldwork close-out and initial findings draft shared.

· Kenya quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Kenya dataset.

4\. Analysis & Validation – Weeks 7–9

Key activities

· Clean, code and analyze quantitative and qualitative data.

· Triangulate findings across methods and countries.

· Develop and populate indicator baseline values.

· Prepare and conduct validation workshop with IsraAID/programme stakeholders.

Deliverables

· Analyzed datasets.

· Populated indicator baseline table.

· Draft findings.

· Validation workshop summary.

5\. Reporting & Dissemination – Weeks 9–10

Key activities

· Incorporate feedback from IsraAID.

· Finalize evaluation/baseline report.

· Prepare executive summary/brief and presentation deck.

· Present findings to relevant stakeholders.

· Hand over final datasets, tools and supporting documentation.

Deliverables

· Final report in MS Word and PDF.

· Executive summary/brief.

· Presentation deck.

· Final clean datasets and tools.

Summary of Key Milestones

· Week 1: Inception phase completed

· Week 2 & 3: Tools finalised/piloted and field preparation completed

· Week 4 & 5: Uganda fieldwork completed

· Weeks 6 & 7: Kenya fieldwork completed and initial Uganda finding draft

· Weeks 8 & 9: Analysis and validation completed; draft report ready

· Week 10: Final report, presentation and data/tools handover completed

Note: The timeline is indicative and may be adjusted in consultation with IsraAID, provided the overall 10-week period and Uganda-to-Kenya sequencing are maintained. Analysis may overlap with final data cleaning. IsraAID will want to be provided access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected, to enable ongoing data quality checks and early identification of gaps or issues.

Summary of Key Baseline Deliverables

· Inception report by the consultant within one (1) week upon signing of the consultancy contract.

· Draft Baseline Survey report with clear findings in line with the aim and outcomes of the programme, conclusion, and recommendations for review.

· Final Baseline Survey report in electronic format (MS Word as well as PDF)

· Summary of the findings in (MS PowerPoint) to be used for subsequent dissemination.

· All raw data: transcripts from In-depth Interviews, Individual Surveys, FGDs and cleaned data set used for analysis and production of the final report in an acceptable electronic format shared on a rolling basis.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

IsraAID and the Programme Team

· Draw the contract and manage its implementation within the period.

· Coordinate the baseline study

· Share relevant documentation that are important for this assignment

· Introduction of the consultant and team to the relevant bodies within the study locations.

· Organize a validation meeting for the baseline findings.

· Review and approve the deliverables presented by the consultant.

Consultant

· Recruit, contract, remunerate, train, coordinate, and supervise data collectors, ensuring compliance with the agreed methodology, ethical standards, data quality requirements, and timelines.

· Lead consultancy assignment including data collection and analysis.

· Develop and review the data collection tools.

· Lead the development of the consultancy report and incorporate any feedback from IsraAID

· Ensure all deliverables of the assignment are accomplished and approved by IsraAID

· Present findings to the IsraAID team and relevant stakeholders for validation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

title: 23451 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA) (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

ICT Systems Integration Technician EFMS/CARLOG
body:
Overview of position

CTG is looking for an ICT Systems Integration Technician EFMS/CARLOG to support its client operation, administration, integration, maintenance, and modernization of the UN mission Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS) utilizing the CARLOG platform. The incumbent will be responsible for the administration and operational support of fleet technology systems, fuel monitoring systems, SQL databases, GPS tracking infrastructure, CAN Bus integrations, and related transport technology solutions.

The objective of the assignment is to ensure the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System and its interoperability with Umoja ERP, Transport Management systems, Fuel Management Enhancement Solutions, and other approved services.

The incumbent will maintain fleet technology infrastructure, vehicle monitoring systems, receiving stations, communication networks, databases, and operational reporting systems while supporting fleet oversight, operational compliance, fuel management, investigations, data analytics, and platform modernization initiatives.

Role objectives

Within delegated authority, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties:

A. EFMS / CARLOG Administration and Operations

Administer, configure, maintain, and support the CARLOG Electronic Fleet Management System (EFMS).

Maintain CARLOG databases, SQL Server environments, and associated applications.

Manage fleet master data including vehicles, drivers, devices, users, and organizational structures.

Create, modify, suspend, and maintain user accounts, permissions, and access privileges.

Maintain the World Fleet Log platform, including reporting and access administration.

Manage CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi devices and ensure their continuous operation.

Monitor system performance, synchronization services, scheduled jobs, and data transmission activities.

Establish and maintain backup, recovery, and business continuity procedures.

Maintain system documentation, architecture diagrams, asset inventories, and technical records.

Coordinate with the client sections, E-Drive Technology (EDT), vendors, and internal stakeholders on technical support activities.

Ensure completeness, integrity, and accuracy of fleet monitoring data.

B. Systems Integration and Platform Modernization

Maintain reliable and secure integration between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and other approved platforms.

Monitor and support automated data exchange and synchronization processes.

Validate interface configurations and ensure proper data flow between integrated systems.

Support modernization initiatives and migration from legacy CARLOG environments to web-based platforms.

Assist with requirements analysis, configuration, testing, data migration, deployment, stabilization, and user adoption activities.

Maintain integration documentation and interface inventories.

C. Receiving Station Administration

Establish, administer, maintain, and support all CARLOG Receiving Stations throughout the mission area.

Monitor receiving station availability, communications, data downloads, and synchronization performance.

Ensure continuous connectivity between receiving stations and CARLOG servers.

Troubleshoot hardware, software, communications, network, and synchronization failures.

Perform system restoration and recovery activities following communication outages.

Maintain operational records and performance statistics for all receiving stations.

D. Fleet Monitoring and Operational Compliance

Monitor and track mission vehicles using CARLOG systems.

Monitor real-time vehicle movements, deployment activities, and utilization patterns.

Analyze vehicle operational performance and fleet usage trends.

Monitor speeding violations, unsafe driving practices, and road safety compliance.

Monitor unauthorized vehicle movements, curfew violations, and misuse of assets.

Investigate vehicle activity anomalies and driver behavior irregularities.

Monitor excessive idling and operational inefficiencies.

Generate alerts, notifications, and operational compliance reports.

Maintain fleet performance indicators and statistical data.

E. Fuel Management and Monitoring

Monitor fuel consumption, fuel efficiency, and fuel-system performance.

Analyze fuel monitoring data generated through CARLOG and Fuel Management Enhancement systems.

Investigate fuel anomalies, unauthorized fuel usage, fuel loss, and suspected theft incidents.

Validate fuel performance indicators and consumption trends.

Support fuel-related investigations and corrective actions.

Produce fuel consumption, efficiency, and utilization reports.

F. Vehicle Systems Integration and Diagnostics

Review vehicle technical manuals, wiring diagrams, and electronic documentation.

Analyze vehicle communication networks including CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU interfaces.

Support installation, configuration, calibration, and validation of CARLOG devices and vehicle integrations.

Configure data acquisition from vehicle electronic control units.

Support mechanics, electricians, workshop staff, and installation teams during deployments.

Diagnose communication, electrical, and integration faults.

Verify compliance with CARLOG installation standards.

Perform testing and operational acceptance of installations and upgrades.

G. SIM Card and Communication Management

Administer and monitor active SIM cards supporting CARLOG live communications.

Maintain communication performance and monitor transmission quality.

Coordinate activation, replacement, provisioning, and troubleshooting activities with the section and service providers.

Maintain SIM card inventories, assignment records, subscriptions, and data plans.

Resolve communication outages and connectivity disruptions.

Ensure uninterrupted transmission of vehicle data to fleet monitoring platforms.

H. Monitoring, Incident Resolution and Service Support

Monitor application availability, server performance, interfaces, synchronization services, logs, and exception queues.

Investigate incidents and restore services within agreed service levels.

Provide Level 1 and Level 2 technical support to users.

Maintain complete incident records, root-cause analyses, and resolution documentation.

Escalate unresolved issues appropriately and coordinate corrective actions.

Support system upgrades, patching, and maintenance activities.

I. Data Quality and Reconciliation

Validate vehicle, driver, fuel, trip, maintenance, mileage, and operational data.

Perform data reconciliation between CARLOG, Umoja ERP, and other integrated systems.

Investigate inconsistencies and data anomalies.

Coordinate corrective actions with stakeholders and business owners.

Maintain data quality standards and reporting accuracy.

J. Reporting, Business Intelligence and Analytics

Generate and distribute:

Daily fleet monitoring reports.

Weekly and monthly operational reports.

Vehicle movement and utilization reports.

Management dashboards and KPI reports.

Driver behavior and road safety reports.

Curfew violation and compliance reports.

Fuel consumption and efficiency reports.

Fuel anomaly and investigation reports.

Receiving station performance reports.

Fleet deployment and operational readiness reports.

Annual mileage audit reports.

Historical vehicle activity reports.

Statistical reports for the CTO and Transport Management.

Data-driven recommendations to improve fleet efficiency, safety, compliance, and resource utilization.

K. Investigation and Compliance Support

Support Safety and Investigations Unit (SIU) inquiries and transport-related investigations.

Analyze vehicle movement histories and reconstruct routes.

Produce evidence-based reports using CARLOG data.

Support accident investigations and vehicle misuse assessments.

Monitor compliance with transport regulations, policies, and operational procedures.

Provide analytical support for management decision-making.

L. Workshop and Maintenance Support

Support vehicle maintenance management activities.

Maintain vehicle maintenance records within CARLOG.

Monitor maintenance schedules and vehicle service status.

Ensure maintenance activities are accurately recorded.

Support vehicle diagnostics and troubleshooting activities.

Assist in identifying technical faults and reducing unnecessary parts replacement through accurate analysis.

M. Security, Change and Release Management

Apply role-based access control and user security management.

Implement approved system changes, upgrades, configurations, and releases.

Maintain audit trails, access records, and security documentation.

Support testing, validation, rollback procedures, and change-control processes.

Ensure compliance with applicable UN ICT security standards and policies.

N. Training, Knowledge Management and Stakeholder Coordination

Deliver technical and user training on CARLOG, EFMS, fleet monitoring systems, and related technologies.

Develop technical procedures, user guides, and training materials.

Conduct knowledge-transfer sessions and support user adoption initiatives.

Provide vehicle tracking support to the Security Operations Centre (SOC).

Liaise with Transport, ICT, IT section, Finance, Supply Chain, Fuel Management personnel, vendors, and service providers.

Maintain knowledge repositories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and technical documentation.

Perform other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Monthly Deliverables

Monthly service-performance report covering system availability, incidents, service requests, recurring problems, changes implemented, outstanding risks, and corrective actions.

Fleet monitoring report covering vehicle utilization, operational compliance, driver behavior, curfew violations, and fleet performance indicators.

Fuel monitoring and reconciliation report covering fuel consumption trends, anomalies, investigations, and corrective actions.

Integration and data-quality report covering CARLOG, Umoja ERP, Transport systems, Fuel Management Enhancement solutions, and related interfaces.

CARLOG modernization status report covering migration progress, testing, deployment readiness, user adoption, and stabilization activities.

Receiving station performance report covering availability, connectivity, synchronization status, and maintenance activities.

Updated technical documentation, system inventories, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and knowledge articles.

Training and knowledge-transfer report identifying sessions delivered, participants, materials used, and follow-up actions.

Forward work plan outlining priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, and resource requirements for the following month.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Education

High school diploma or equivalent is required.

Technical training in Information Technology, Electronics, Telematics, Automotive Technology, Fleet Management Systems, Vehicle Diagnostics, Computer Science, Transport Technology, or related disciplines is required.

A university degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, Electronics, Automotive Engineering, Transport Management, or a related field is desirable.

Work Experience

A minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in fleet management, fleet monitoring, telematics systems, transport operations, fuel management systems, vehicle tracking technologies, or comparable operational systems in a multi-site environment.

Demonstrated experience in the administration and support of Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS), GPS tracking platforms, telematics solutions, and fleet-monitoring applications.

Practical experience in systems integration, data validation, database administration, incident management, testing, deployment support, and technical documentation.

Experience administering and maintaining SQL databases, fleet management applications, and reporting systems.

Proven experience with CAN Bus integration, vehicle communication protocols (OBD-II, J1939, LIN), vehicle diagnostics, and automotive electrical systems.

Experience maintaining vehicle communication networks, monitoring devices, fuel monitoring systems, and related fleet technology infrastructure.

Experience supporting large and geographically dispersed vehicle fleets of 500 vehicles or more is highly desirable.

Experience supporting web-based application deployments, platform upgrades, or migrations from legacy client/server environments is highly desirable.

Knowledge of CARLOG, World Fleet Log, Umoja ERP, UN transport operations, fuel management systems, or comparable fleet-management platforms is highly desirable.

Experience within the United Nations, military, government, humanitarian, peacekeeping, or other international organizations is an advantage.

Demonstrated ability to analyze operational data, produce management reports, and support evidence-based decision-making through fleet analytics and performance monitoring.

Technical Skills

CARLOG Fleet Monitoring System Administration

Electronic Fleet Management Systems (EFMS)

World Fleet Log Platform Administration

Fleet Telematics and Vehicle Tracking Technologies

GPS Monitoring and Geolocation Systems

Microsoft SQL Server Administration and Database Management

Database Design, Querying, Data Validation, and Reporting

Systems Integration and Data Synchronization

Umoja ERP Interface Support and Data Reconciliation

CAN Bus, J1939, OBD-II, LIN, and ECU Communications

Vehicle Diagnostics and Automotive Electronic Systems

CARLOG F1 3G and F2 LTE/Wi-Fi Device Administration

Fuel Monitoring Systems and Fuel Analytics

SIM Card, GSM, LTE, and Mobile Data Connectivity Management

Receiving Station Administration and Communications Management

Server Administration, Performance Monitoring, and Troubleshooting

Incident Management and Technical Support

Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, and Dashboard Development

Microsoft Excel (Advanced)

Microsoft Power BI

Technical Documentation and Knowledge Management

Technical Reporting, Fleet Analytics, and Performance Measurement

Change Management, Testing, Deployment, and Release Support

Information Security, Access Control, and Audit Compliance

Team management

This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are strongly advised to apply.

title: Junior Project Assistant
body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

**Organizational Context and Scope**

Under the direct supervision of the project manager and under the guidance of the Head of Unit for Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI) and under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission in the Country Office for Belgium and Luxembourg, the incumbent will assist the LMI team with the implementation of projects of the IOM Country Office. In addition to this, the incumbent will be expected to support some activities related to the development of new projects in the LMI Team.

**Responsibilities**

In particular, the incumbent will:

  
I. ASSIST WITH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS

1\. In close coordination with the LMI Head of Unit, assist the Project Management Teams with the implementation and follow-up on project activities. This includes supporting the team with research tasks, administrative tasks and the (logistical) organization of meetings and events.   
2\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of reports; routine correspondence, type letters, reports and memoranda as well as IOM documents and forms related to IOM operational and administrative matters;   
3\. Assist the Project Management Team with the development of new projects and initiatives in the field of Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion. This includes assistance with the drafting/ formatting of concept notes and project proposals.   
4\. Assist in drafting/ formatting public information documents, website articles, press releases and information dissemination on IOM activities towards public and private stakeholders.   
5\. Any other tasks as may be required.

  
II- ASSIST WITH POLICY SUPPORT AND OUTREACH

6\. Assist in identifying possible partnerships with the private sector, civil society (NGOs, diaspora associations, etc.) and other stakeholders (such as the Belgian government and universities) in order to improve knowledge on migration initiatives and policies.   
7\. Assist with the drafting/ formatting of presentations and speeches related to integration for the LMI Head of Unit or the Chief of Mission.   
8\. Prepare for, participate in and follow-up on meetings/conferences on behalf of the organization.   
9\. Any other tasks as may be required.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

**•**  Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in economics, social science, migration studies or related field from an accredited academic institution with one year of relevant professional experience.   
OR   
• Completed High School degree with three years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of project management, or evaluation of projects;   
• Demonstrated first working experience or internship in the area of migrant integration or labour migration;   
• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Ability to work independently;   
• Experience in liaison with non-governmental organizations, national, regional and international authorities and institutions is an advantage.

**Skills**

• Strong organizational and time-management skills;   
• Strong communication and diplomatic skills, applied in a professional environment;   
• Ability to work independently against tight deadlines.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Advanced knowledge of Dutch is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators Level 1

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers.
